items.title: A Sixfold Staging: From Bare Capacity to Ultimate Completion

items.zh: 當知此中，如是一切補特伽羅，六位所攝。何等為六？一、有堪能補特伽羅，二、成就下品善根補特伽羅，三、成就中品善根補特伽羅，四、成就上品善根補特伽羅，五、究竟方便補特伽羅，六、已到究竟補特伽羅。云何堪能補特伽羅？謂安住種姓補特伽羅，而未獲得最初於佛正覺正說法毘奈耶所有正信，廣說乃至調柔諸見。是名堪能補特伽羅。云何成就下品善根補特伽羅？謂安住種姓補特伽羅，已能獲得最初於佛正覺正說法毘奈耶所有正信，廣說乃至調柔諸見。
items.en: It should be understood that all such persons are comprised within six positions. What are the six? A person of capacity; a person who has attained a lower grade of wholesome roots; a person who has attained a middle grade of wholesome roots; a person who has attained a higher grade of wholesome roots; a person at the ultimate means; and a person who has reached the ultimate. What is a person of capacity? It is a person abiding in lineage who has not yet attained the very first pure faith in the Dharma and discipline rightly taught by the perfectly awakened Buddha — and so on at length, down to taming and softening [wrong] views. This is called a person of capacity. What is a person who has attained a lower grade of wholesome roots? It is a person abiding in lineage who has already attained that very first pure faith in the Dharma and discipline rightly taught by the perfectly awakened Buddha — and so on at length, down to taming and softening [wrong] views.

items.zh: 是名成就下品善根補特伽羅。
items.en: This is called a person who possesses a lower grade of wholesome roots.

items.title: The Sixfold Staging Completes: Middle and Upper Roots, Ultimate Means, and the Ultimate Itself

items.zh: 云何成就中品善根補特伽羅？謂安住種姓補特伽羅，已能獲得最初於佛正覺正說法毘奈耶所有正信，廣說乃至調柔諸見；從是已後，或經一生，或二、或多，展轉勝進，而未獲得最後有身。謂住於此能般涅槃，或能趣入正性離生。是名成就中品善根補特伽羅。云何成就上品善根補特伽羅？謂即如是展轉勝進補特伽羅，已能獲得最後有身。若住於此能般涅槃，或能趣入正性離生。是名成就上品善根補特伽羅。云何名為究竟方便補特伽羅？謂已獲得最後有身補特伽羅，為盡諸漏聽聞正法，或得無倒教授教誡，正修加行，而未能得遍一切種諸漏永盡，未到究竟。如是名為究竟方便補特伽羅。云何名為已到究竟補特伽羅？謂即如是補特伽羅，為盡諸漏聽聞正法，獲得無倒教授教誡，如是如是正修加行，已能獲得遍一切種諸漏永盡，所作已辦，究竟獲得第一清涼。如是名為已到究竟補特伽羅。當知此中，堪能種類補特伽羅，即以種姓為依為住，便能獲得下品善根，及能趣入。既趣入已，下品善根為依為住，復能獲得中品善根，以此善根而自成熟。彼於如是自成熟時，中品善根為依為住，復能獲得上品善根，已得成熟。彼由如是上品善根修集為因所得自體，復能修集轉勝資糧。由是觸證心一境性，復能趣入正性離生，證預流果、或一來果、或不還果，而未能證最勝第一阿羅漢果。如是名為究竟方便補特伽羅。若已證得一切煩惱皆悉永斷阿羅漢果，爾時名為已到究竟補特伽羅。此則顯示由初中後一切聲聞所修正行，所立六種補特伽羅。由有種姓聲聞正行，顯示最初補特伽羅；由到究竟聲聞正行，顯示最後補特伽羅；由餘聲聞所修正行，顯示中間補特伽羅。
items.en: What is a person who has attained a middle grade of wholesome roots? …From this point onward, whether over one lifetime, two, or many, becoming progressively more excellent, yet not having obtained the final body of existence. …What is a person who has attained a higher grade of wholesome roots? It is this same person, having become progressively more excellent, who has now obtained the final body of existence. …What is called a person at the ultimate means? It is a person who, having obtained the final body of existence, in order to exhaust all outflows, hears the true Dharma … yet is not yet able to exhaust every kind of outflow entirely, not yet having reached the ultimate. What is called a person who has reached the ultimate? It is this same person who, in order to exhaust all outflows, hears the true Dharma, obtains undistorted instruction and admonition, and, practising accordingly, is now able to exhaust every kind of outflow entirely — the task is done, the ultimate, foremost coolness finally attained. …A person of the capable kind, resting on and abiding in lineage itself, is thereby able to obtain the lower grade of wholesome roots, and to enter. Having entered, resting on and abiding in the lower grade, one is further able to obtain the middle grade, and by means of this ripens oneself. At the time of this self-ripening, resting on and abiding in the middle grade, one is further able to obtain the higher grade, and ripening is complete. By means of this cultivation of the higher grade as cause, one obtains a [transformed] basis of existence, and is further able to cultivate the still more excellent provisions. By this, one touches and realises one-pointedness of mind, and is further able to enter correct nature free of afflictive arising, attaining the fruit of stream-entry, or once-returning, or non-returning — yet not yet attaining the foremost fruit of arhatship. …If one has already attained arhatship, in which every affliction is permanently cut off, at that time one is called a person who has reached the ultimate.

items.title: Section: Establishment Closes — How Long Does Entry Actually Take?

items.zh: 問：已得趣入補特伽羅，為有定量，一切時等得般涅槃？為無定量，一切時分而不齊等得般涅槃？答：無有定量，亦非一切時分齊等得般涅槃。然隨所應，如所遇緣有差別故，而般涅槃。當知此中，或有一類極經久遠，或有一類非極久遠，或有一類最極速疾得般涅槃。謂住種姓補特伽羅，最極速疾般涅槃者，要經三生。第一生中，最初趣入；第二生中，修令成熟；第三生中，修成熟已。或即此身得般涅槃，或若不得般涅槃者，必入學位，方可夭沒，極經七有得般涅槃。如是名為趣入安立。
items.en: Question: For a person who has already entered, is there a fixed measure — do all attain nirvāṇa in an equal span of time? Or is there no fixed measure, such that the time is not equal for all? Answer: There is no fixed measure, nor do all attain nirvāṇa in an equal span of time. …It should be understood that among such persons, some take an extremely long time, some take a time that is not extremely long, and some attain nirvāṇa most swiftly of all. …For a person abiding in lineage who attains nirvāṇa most swiftly, three lifetimes are required. In the first lifetime, initial entry occurs; in the second lifetime, practice brings one to the verge of ripening; in the third lifetime, having ripened through practice, one either attains nirvāṇa in this very body, or, if not, one will certainly enter the stage of a trainee before this life ends, attaining nirvāṇa after, at most, seven further rounds of rebirth. This is called the establishment of entry.

blocks.text: How does a person move from bare capacity to the goal, and how long does it take?

items: **Capacity**: one who has the seed but has not begun. Venerable Miào Jìng: "whether doing good or evil, going to the heavens or the lower realms, this uncontaminated seed abides unmoved."
**Lower-grade wholesome roots**: Master Cháng Bǎi: this is what is first attained, called "having entered".
**The ultimate means**: Master Cháng Bǎi: the process is the "means", the result the "ultimate"; the seven noble persons short of arhatship are on the ultimate means.
**The ultimate**: the arhat. Venerable Miào Jìng: "arhat" is also rendered "the unattached".

blocks.text: "For a person in lineage who attains nirvāṇa most swiftly, three lifetimes are required: in the first, initial entry; in the second, ripening; in the third, liberation." Venerable Miào Jìng: if calm succeeds, and one practises the foundations of mindfulness within it, one could attain stream-entry in this life. After stream-entry, at most seven existences remain. Master Cháng Bǎi: seven existences means up to fourteen births, human and heavenly alternately.

Three lifetimes at the very fastest. The treatise is not discouraging; it is realistic. Venerable Miào Jìng's point is that each life counts: the seeds planted now determine how quickly the next steps come.

quiz.q: Into which six positions does the treatise gather all persons?
options: capacity; lower, middle, and higher wholesome roots; ultimate means; reached the ultimate
quiz.why: The six: a person of capacity; one with lower-grade wholesome roots; middle-grade; higher-grade; one at the ultimate means; and one who has reached the ultimate. Venerable Miào Jìng: "position" means grade — the order of depth.

quiz.q: The note says the six positions subdivide "about to ripen." How does Master Cháng Bǎi map the grades onto entry and ripening?
options: lower grade = entered; higher grade = ripened; middle grade = about to ripen
all three are about to ripen
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: what such a being first attains is the lower grade of wholesome roots — this is called having entered. And: in the classification by dharmas it is the fourth, already ripened; by persons, the third — the already-ripened person belongs to the higher grade. This differs from the note.

quiz.q: The "person of capacity" has not yet gained faith. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say of his uncontaminated seed?
options: whether doing good or evil, rising or falling, the uncontaminated seed abides unmoved
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: whether doing good or evil, going to the heavens or to the three lower realms, this uncontaminated seed abides unmoved.

quiz.q: What range do the masters give for the "person at the ultimate means"?
options: Cháng Bǎi: the process is means, the result ultimate — the seven noble ones before arhatship; Miào Jìng: it indicates non-return and the approach to arhatship
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the process is the "means," the result the "ultimate"; on the way to the ultimate it is called the ultimate means — the seven noble ones before arhatship. Venerable Miào Jìng: this indicates having reached non-return and the approach to arhatship, but not yet arhatship. The ranges differ.

quiz.q: The one who has reached the ultimate "attains the foremost coolness." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say "arhat" is also translated as?
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: with no clinging at all — the state of non-attachment — so "arhat" is also translated as "the unattached."

quiz.q: How many lifetimes does the treatise say even the swiftest lineage-bearer needs to attain nirvāṇa?
options: three — entering in the first, ripening in the second, and in the third attaining nirvāṇa or entering the trainee stage, at most seven more existences
quiz.why: "For a person abiding in lineage who attains nirvāṇa most swiftly, three lifetimes are required. In the first, initial entry; in the second, ripening; in the third, having ripened, one either attains nirvāṇa in this body" or enters the trainee stage.

quiz.q: Why three lifetimes at the fastest, and not two, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: one must wait for a buddha
if calm were achieved in the second life, stream-entry would come then; but the second life only reaches the inner ordinary stage without concentration, so a third is needed
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: if calm-abiding succeeded, practising the four foundations within it you should attain stream-entry in that life — then two lives would suffice. But in the second life one only reaches the inner ordinary stage without calm, so three are needed.
